concept: Pre-quantized BinData vector ingestion (int8 and int1) in MongoDB
summary: Source-anchored research for Pre-quantized BinData vector ingestion (int8 and int1) in MongoDB. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Packing preserves logical vector dimensions: 1024 binary dimensions occupy 128 payload bytes. Configure numDimensions as 1024, not 128. Packed-bit bytes contain eight dimensions each; they must not be interpreted as 128 scalar int8 dimensions. (high confidence) Sources: https://docs.cohere.com/docs/embeddings ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/vector-quantization.md ; https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/bson-binary-vector/bson-binary-vector.md

Quantizing float32 payloads gives nominal 4x compression for int8 and 32x for packed bits, before metadata and index overhead. MongoDB's HNSW graph does not shrink with vector values. Therefore those payload ratios must not be presented as whole-cluster RAM, bill, or consolidation TCO reductions. (high confidence)

For pre-quantized ingestion, serialize query vectors to the same BinData element dtype as stored vectors and use the same embedding model. Sending full-fidelity query vectors to int8/int1 fields is not the automatic-quantization query path; the stage reference warns that incompatible subtypes can produce empty results without an error. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

MongoDB Vector Search can ingest and index pre-quantized int8 and int1 embeddings stored as BSON BinData. Quantization happens before insertion; unlike automatic index quantization, this can reduce both mongod document storage and mongot index memory. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

BSON binary subtype 9 identifies a vector; int8 and packed-bit/int1 are element dtypes within that subtype. A generic binary blob or ordinary integer array is not the same representation. Drivers serialize dtype and padding metadata before the packed values. (high confidence)

The vector storage format is BSON binary subtype 9. Its internal element dtype identifies INT8 (0x03), FLOAT32 (0x27), or PACKED_BIT (0x10); int1 is the search documentation's name for packed-bit vectors, not a separate BSON binary subtype number. (high confidence) Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/bson-binary-vector/bson-binary-vector.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/vector-quantization.md

The documented pre-quantized int1 ingestion path requires a dimension count divisible by eight and supports euclidean similarity only. Pre-quantized int8 supports cosine, euclidean, and dotProduct. The vectorSearch index dimension ceiling is 8192. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

For a vectorSearch index that ingests pre-quantized vectors, omit fields.quantization or set it to none. Setting scalar or binary invokes automatic quantization of floating-point input; int8/int1 BinData inputs can then be silently skipped. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/vector-quantization.md

Storing only pre-quantized vectors does not preserve an original full-precision copy for MongoDB's built-in float rescoring. Retaining another float32 field and indexing it with automatic binary quantization is a documented alternative, but changes the storage assumptions of a cost comparison. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

Java ingestion can wrap scalar bytes with BinaryVector.int8Vector(byte[]) and packed bits with BinaryVector.packedBitVector(byte[], padding); the reference implementation uses distinct fields for the two encodings. (high confidence)

Quantization quality depends on the embedding model and preprocessing. Hugging Face reports substantial losses for some models and explains that int8 calibration data determines quantization buckets. Successful ingestion alone does not establish that a model's quantized embeddings preserve retrieval quality. (high confidence)

Cohere documents float, int8, uint8, binary, and ubinary embedding outputs and allows multiple types in one Embed API call. This is upstream output capability, not proof that every output type is directly compatible with MongoDB BSON vector dtypes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

Cohere documents int8, uint8, binary, and ubinary embedding outputs. For MongoDB ingestion, choose a compatible representation: signed int8 values map to INT8, while unsigned packed binary bytes map to PACKED_BIT. Do not treat every provider's integer-valued output as interchangeable. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) Sources: https://docs.cohere.com/docs/embeddings ; https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/bson-binary-vector/bson-binary-vector.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/vector-quantization.md

MongoDB's Node.js example serializes signed byte embeddings with Binary.fromInt8Array(new Int8Array(...)) and already-packed unsigned binary bytes with Binary.fromPackedBits(new Uint8Array(...)). These operations encode provider output into subtype 9; they are distinct from generating or calibrating quantized embeddings. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

BSON PACKED_BIT encoding permits a padding count from zero to seven, but the documented MongoDB Vector Search int1 ingestion path requires dimensions divisible by eight. A vector accepted by a driver's binary encoder therefore need not satisfy search-index dimensionality constraints. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/bson-binary-vector/bson-binary-vector.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/vector-quantization.md
